Palanga Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Palanga, Lithuania

Demolished. Palanga's Jewish community likely dates to the second half of the 15th century, with burial records from the local Hevra Kadisha confirmed as early as 1487. As a Baltic seaside resort town, Jews here worked prominently in the amber trade and resort businesses, helping make Palanga Lithuania's premier summer destination; many held city administration roles during the interwar period. A 1938 fire destroyed most of the Jewish residential quarter. This original cemetery stood near the entrance to the Tiškevičius family park; when the park was established, archaeologists found burial layers over 200 years old beneath it, though no marker of the cemetery survives there today. From 1831, burial records shifted to a newer cemetery near Naglis Hill, which itself stopped being used after the 1941 Holocaust massacre that killed over 300 of Palanga's Jews. Notable resident Yudel Mark (1897-1975), a prominent Yiddish linguist, was born in Palanga. A 1991 memorial stone in Yiddish, Hebrew, and Lithuanian now marks the old cemetery's former location; the newer cemetery was added to Lithuania's Cultural Property Register in 2008.
